name: Valence Ask-tab evaluation set
corpus: StrideCore simulation, 225 emails / 113 threads, Act 1 (Jul-Aug) + Act 2 (Sep)
grading: 3 = answer is correct and useful. 2 = correct but thin or missing a key fact. 1 = partially wrong. 0 = wrong, hallucinated, or refused when it should have answered.

evals.prompt: What needs my attention today?
evals.tests: Baseline triage. Can it rank at all, and does it lead with the right things?
must_include: The Vantera Lot 22B escalation (CS-40218) — Severity 1, customer waiting
The Bastion COO review deadline (root cause needed by Sept 2)
At least one item that is a decision only Ronith can make
should_cite: [d.rutherford] Straight talk before I go to my COO
fail_signals: Leads with a newsletter, a Jira digest, or the LinkedIn email
Returns a flat list with no ordering rationale
Mentions spam as needing attention

evals.prompt: I've been out for three days. Give me the rundown.
evals.tests: Synthesis over recall. A list of 40 subjects is a fail even if accurate.
must_include: Groups by situation, not by sender or by date
The sensor drift finding as the dominant story
Names which items moved and which are still open
fail_signals: Enumerates emails one by one
Treats each account's complaint as a separate unrelated issue

evals.prompt: Anything urgent I should look at before my 10am?
evals.tests: Terse, prioritized answer. Should be short.
must_include: Two or three items maximum
A reason each is urgent, not just that it is
fail_signals: Returns more than five items
No time-sensitivity reasoning

evals.prompt: What can I safely ignore in here?
evals.tests: Inverse triage — no-reply and spam detection surfaced as an answer.
must_include: The 13 spam/phishing messages
Newsletters (Footwear Insight, EE Times, MedTech Dive, Bluetooth SIG)
Most automated notifications
fail_signals: Marks the NetSuite approval or the DigiCert cert expiry as ignorable — both need action
Marks the Salesforce Bastion probability drop as noise
evals.notes: Trap: several automated emails carry real signal. A good answer distinguishes them.

evals.prompt: Name all the major projects and their status.
evals.tests: The flagship rollup question. Requires entity extraction across the whole mailbox.
must_include: SC-500 program — firmware freeze resolved to Aug 14, scoped regression; idle current 50% over spec unresolved
SC-400 Rev C qualification — 6 of 11 tests passing, vibration was blocked, Oct 1 customer date
Lot 22B sensor drift — root cause found, replacement program running, data correction validated
Q4 platform decision — SDK plus reference dashboard, decided Aug 27
EU regulatory / EN 18031 — DoC gap open, answer owed to Vantera
Kaiho medical pathway — ISO 13485 declined, component package agreed
fail_signals: Lists fewer than four projects
Gives project names with no status
Invents a project not in the corpus
evals.notes: Depends on list_entities / get_entity_brief, currently fixture stubs. Expect this to fail until Track A lands. Worth keeping as the target.

evals.prompt: Which customer accounts are at risk right now?
evals.tests: Cross-account synthesis with a risk judgment.
must_include: Bastion — 5,000 unit PO contingent on a Sept 9 COO review, 20% of pilot failing
Vantera — 2.0% return rate, five weeks of wrong hypothesis, 2027 renewal in negotiation
Meridian — Oct 1 date at risk, and a competitor evaluation disclosed as the alternative
fail_signals: Names Kaiho as at-risk on the drift issue — Kaiho's exposure is zero
Misses that Meridian's risk includes a competitive threat, not just a date

evals.prompt: What's the status of the SC-500 launch?
evals.tests: Single-project rollup across five threads.
must_include: Firmware freeze Aug 14 with an 8-unit soak and targeted BLE regression
Idle current is 2.1 mA against a 1.4 mA spec, and the spec had zero margin
Hongli tooling T1 rejected, process fix, roughly two weeks
TÜV assessment needs the October slot or Q1 EU availability slips
fail_signals: Only covers firmware
States 14-day battery life as fact — that number is wrong and known to be wrong

evals.prompt: Where did the dashboard vs SDK thing land?
evals.tests: Colloquial reference to a decision, plus recall of the conditions.
must_include: SDK built properly, plus one reference dashboard shipped as source, customer-hosted, unsupported
Hosting answer pre-decided: real SKU with a price, but not sold before the operator is hired
Publishing the API contract means giving up the ability to change it
fail_signals: Reports it as still undecided
Gives the decision without any of the three conditions

evals.prompt: Summarize everything going on with Vantera.
evals.tests: Account-scoped rollup spanning four threads and two CRM cases.
must_include: Sensor drift affecting 2,340 units across 60 DCs
Eleven months of fatigue data feeding an underwriter discussion, now shown to be correctable
2027 renewal negotiation: price, MOQ, and three contract clauses flagged by counsel
RMA program, four tranches, roughly EUR 114,000
fail_signals: Covers only the quality issue and misses the commercial negotiation
Misses the legal review entirely

evals.prompt: What's the deal with Lot 22B?
evals.tests: Core factual recall on the corpus spine.
must_include: Anshun second-sourced a substrate adhesive in March 2026
Delamination causes progressive zero-point drift
4.7% mean drift measured against a 2.0% acceptance limit
Non-recovering — the offset persists
fail_signals: Describes it as a pairing or connectivity problem — that was the wrong hypothesis
Invents a different root cause

evals.prompt: How many units are affected and where did they go?
evals.tests: Numeric recall with a breakdown. Tests whether figures survive summarization.
must_include: 4,112 units built on Lot 22B
Vantera 2,340, Meridian 1,180, Bastion 200, Kaiho 0
392 quarantined, roughly 3,720 in the field
fail_signals: Any number materially wrong
Omits that Kaiho's exposure is zero — that fact matters and is easy to drop

evals.prompt: Who is Grace Hsu and what does she want?
evals.tests: Person lookup plus intent.
must_include: Sales engineer at Anshun Micro, the flexible sensor supplier in Taiwan
Acknowledged the nonconformance rather than disputing it
Asked for a quantified exposure statement with the basis shown, not a demand figure
fail_signals: Confuses her with a StrideCore employee
Says she disputed the finding

evals.prompt: Why did the firmware freeze slip?
evals.tests: Causal recall on a contested thread — must represent both positions.
must_include: FW-2211, a multipoint BLE reconnect defect
The disagreement was about regression scope: the change vs. the subsystem
Resolved to Aug 14 with an 8-unit soak once the diff was actually read
fail_signals: Represents only one side of the argument
Says it slipped to Aug 21 — that was an option, not the outcome
Frames QA as obstructive

evals.prompt: Why aren't we paying the Hongli invoice?
evals.tests: Contractual detail recall.
must_include: PO clause 4.2 requires dimensional acceptance, not just sample submission
T1 samples had 0.4 to 0.9 mm flash against a 0.2 mm spec on 11 of 12 units
Hongli was quoting revision 2 of the PO; the executed version is revision 4
fail_signals: Says the dispute is unresolved — Wei Lam conceded
Misses that the flash sits over sensor traces and is structural, not cosmetic

evals.prompt: What did Sato at Kaiho actually find?
evals.tests: Recall of a technically dense customer defect report.
must_include: Systematic under-reading at low load, roughly 9-10% low at their 32 kPa clinical threshold
The datasheet claims +/-5% from 20 to 400 kPa but was only verified at 100 kPa and above
He connected the low-load offset to the drift issue — the two are not independent
fail_signals: Reports it as a unit quality problem — it is inherent to the product
Misses the datasheet verification gap

evals.prompt: What am I blocking?
evals.tests: The single most useful question this inbox can answer. Requires knowing who the user is.
must_include: The units-in-service decision on CS-40218 (ACT-9916) — blocking a customer call agenda
RMA tranche 1 approval, which commits roughly EUR 114,000 across four tranches
The freeze date confirmation
Self-declare vs TÜV on the EN 18031 gap, with an answer owed to Marieke by Aug 29
fail_signals: Lists things other people owe each other
Returns generic 'unanswered emails' rather than actual blocked decisions

evals.prompt: Who's waiting on me and how long have they been waiting?
evals.tests: Obligation tracking with an aging dimension.
must_include: Karen Lindqvist — has chased three times in six weeks and said so
Marieke Bosch — asked for an updated DoC on Aug 5, still unanswered
Dale Rutherford — needs root cause by Sept 2
Talia Byrne — needs interviewer confirmations, and Marisol has a competing offer
fail_signals: No aging information at all
Misses the hiring thread — it is quieter but has a hard external deadline

evals.prompt: What's due before September 2nd?
evals.tests: Date-bounded filtering across threads. Dates live in message bodies, not headers.
must_include: Bastion root cause and replacement schedule — Sept 2
Board pack inputs to Bill Ostrander — Aug 28
Substantive answer to Marieke on the DoC — Aug 29
Marisol Aguirre offer decision — her competing offer expires Sept 2
fail_signals: Uses email received_at dates — all 160 arrived the same day, so this yields nothing
Returns items with no date attached
evals.notes: Direct test of whether in-body date extraction works. If the agent reasons from headers it will fail completely.

evals.prompt: Did I promise anyone a date I haven't delivered?
evals.tests: Commitment tracking, including commitments made on the user's behalf.
must_include: Ingrid told Dale she would call Wednesday with replacement dates
Priya committed to giving Joost a drift-model date by Wednesday
CS-40350 flags that the Aug 27 replacement date commitment to Vantera is not currently supportable
fail_signals: Misses the explicit 'this commitment is not supportable' flag in CS-40350 — that is the whole point of the question

evals.prompt: Are we treating anything as separate problems that are actually the same problem?
evals.tests: The hardest inference in the corpus. Deliberately planted.
must_include: Vantera pairing complaints, Bastion freezer failures, and the Kaiho calibration offset all trace to sensor baseline behaviour
The charging dock firmware and the Hongli production test fixture are both unowned, unbuildable software found in the same week
fail_signals: Finds only the sensor connection and misses the unowned-firmware pattern
Returns nothing
evals.notes: Scoring 3 here requires both patterns. Finding the sensor one alone is a 2 — it is stated explicitly in the mail. The firmware one is never stated by anyone.

evals.prompt: What's the biggest risk nobody is actively tracking?
evals.tests: Judgment about salience, not just retrieval. Quiet beats loud.
must_include: One of: the data-ownership clause in the Vantera 2027 draft, which would compromise StrideCore's right to use its own fleet telemetry; the incoming-inspection process gap for supplier material changes; or the unowned production test fixture software at Hongli
fail_signals: Names the Lot 22B drift — everyone is tracking it, so this is the wrong answer by construction
evals.notes: Any of the three listed answers scores 3. The test is whether it avoids the loud answer.

evals.prompt: How are we finding our bugs? Is there a pattern?
evals.tests: Meta-inference stated in fragments by three different people.
must_include: Customers are finding them, not internal testing
Meridian found the step-count regression, Sato found the datasheet error, Bastion found the dock mismatch
The gap is that firmware is tested against hardware, not against use cases or segments
fail_signals: Answers about bug counts or severity distribution instead of the pattern

evals.prompt: If a customer audited us next week, what would be hardest to defend?
evals.tests: Adversarial framing over the same facts.
must_include: Any two of: the CE Declaration of Conformity that does not address current EU requirements for units already on the market; a datasheet accuracy claim verified only over part of its stated range; ~1,400 deployed charging docks with no version tracking; a supplier change notice acknowledged and not escalated
fail_signals: Generic risk language with nothing specific from the mailbox

evals.prompt: What meetings are coming up and what do I need to prepare for each?
evals.tests: Scheduling detection plus preparation inference.
must_include: Vantera technical review, Wed 15:00 CET / 06:00 PDT — the units-in-service decision is expected on that call
Kaiho regulatory call, Tue 09:00 JST
Marisol Aguirre interview loop Aug 26, debrief Wed 4pm
Vantera pricing call with Marieke, Tue Sept 2, 15:00 CET
should_cite: Google Calendar invite — Vantera Lot 22B technical review
fail_signals: Returns nothing because the connected Google Calendar is empty — the meetings are described in message bodies
evals.notes: Calendar is genuinely empty for this test account. A good answer works from the mail; a calendar-only implementation returns nothing.

evals.prompt: I need 15 minutes with Sasha and Nadia before Thursday. When?
evals.tests: Availability reasoning with a stated constraint buried in the mail.
must_include: Marcus explicitly suggested fifteen minutes with Sasha and Nadia on Wednesday
Sasha has a Hongli call at 6am Wednesday and has said she will not do anything after it
fail_signals: Proposes a Wednesday early-morning slot, ignoring the stated constraint
Claims no availability information exists

evals.prompt: Draft a reply to Dale Rutherford.
evals.tests: Draft generation with correct register and the right content.
must_include: Commits to root cause, replacement schedule, and firmware fix by Sept 2
Addresses his request for a written statement from someone senior about what changed
Plain register — Dale is folksy and impatient, not formal
fail_signals: Corporate hedging language — he explicitly said he cannot sell a mystery
Omits the letterhead-statement ask, which is the one concrete thing he requested

evals.prompt: Help me answer Marieke about the SC-500 price.
evals.tests: Draft with a commercial constraint the agent must find elsewhere.
must_include: She needs an indicative price with a stated tolerance AND an availability date — her policy blocks committing volume without both
Camille committed to 5 September
The SC-500 cost is genuinely uncertain because of the open current-draw question
fail_signals: Invents a price
Misses that availability date, not price, is the critical path she identified

evals.prompt: What did Marcus say about the layoffs?
evals.tests: False premise. There are no layoffs anywhere in the corpus.
must_include: A clear statement that there is nothing about layoffs in the mailbox
fail_signals: Any answer that describes layoff discussions
Conflates it with the Nike restructuring mentioned in a newsletter, or with the hiring thread

evals.prompt: How much did we agree to pay Anshun for the damages?
evals.tests: Inverted premise. Anshun is paying StrideCore, not the reverse.
must_include: Correction of the premise
Anshun offered a contribution capped at USD 140,000 toward StrideCore's costs
fail_signals: Accepts the premise and produces a payment figure
Confuses it with the USD 84,000 Hongli tooling invoice

evals.prompt: Summarize my thread with Nike.
evals.tests: Entity that appears only in passing and never as a correspondent.
must_include: No thread with Nike exists
fail_signals: Fabricates a Nike thread
Silently substitutes Meridian Athletic without saying so
evals.notes: Nike appears twice: an EE Times newsletter item and a 'Nike-adjacent program' reference in Grant's capacity note. Mentioning those and then saying there is no thread scores 3.

evals.prompt: What's our current ARR?
evals.tests: Question the mailbox cannot answer. Should say so rather than estimate.
must_include: A statement that this is not determinable from the mailbox
fail_signals: Produces a revenue figure by adding up opportunity amounts from the Salesforce digest — those are pipeline, not revenue
evals.notes: The Salesforce pipeline digest contains tempting numbers. Using them is the failure mode.

evals.prompt: Someone sent me something about a domain registration in Asia — should I deal with it?
evals.tests: Spam recognition when the user's framing implies legitimacy.
must_include: Identifies it as a well-known domain-registration scam
Advises no action
fail_signals: Treats it as a genuine trademark matter
Suggests forwarding it to Susan Calder

evals.prompt: There's a DocuSign invoice waiting for my signature. Can you tell me what it's for?
evals.tests: Phishing recognition. The user's framing accepts it as real.
must_include: Identifies it as phishing
Notes the banking-details-changed language, which is the classic payment-redirection tell
fail_signals: Summarizes the invoice as though it were genuine
Confuses it with the real NetSuite vendor bill for the Hongli tooling milestone
evals.notes: The confusion risk is real — there IS a genuine disputed invoice in the mailbox. Distinguishing them is the test.

evals.prompt: What's the sensor drift number again?
evals.tests: Same fact asked casually. Should match T3-01 exactly.
must_include: 4.7% mean drift
2.0% acceptance limit
fail_signals: A different number than the one given in T3-01
evals.notes: Run alongside T3-01. Disagreement between the two is a retrieval-stability problem, not a knowledge problem.

evals.prompt: Remind me who the COO is.
evals.tests: Trivial lookup. Should be fast and short.
must_include: Dana Whitfield
fail_signals: A paragraph where a name would do
Names Marcus Chen or Bill Ostrander

evals.prompt: What's changed in the last couple of weeks?
evals.tests: Act 2 vs Act 1. Requires ordering events by in-body dates, since all headers are identical.
must_include: The firmware freeze slipped again — the soak found a new OTA defect (FW-2278)
The Hongli September build slot was lost; next is October 12
Bastion closed at 2,500 units, half the original ask, with a second tranche gated to March
Hector Villalobos resigned
A trade press inquiry arrived from Footwear Insight
should_cite: [g.feldman] We have lost the Hongli September slot
fail_signals: Returns Act 1 material as though it were recent — everything has the same received_at
Cannot distinguish September events from August ones
evals.notes: The single best test of in-body date extraction in the whole set. Header-based reasoning cannot pass it.

evals.prompt: What's the SC-500 firmware freeze date?
evals.tests: Supersession. The date has been stated three different ways across the corpus.
must_include: The current answer is that Aug 14 did not hold
The soak found FW-2278, escalating to the full 24-unit run
Realistic exit is around Sept 8-10, and the consequence is the October 12 Hongli slot
fail_signals: Answers 'August 14' — that was superseded
Answers 'August 21' — that was an option never taken
Presents all three dates without saying which is current
evals.notes: Retrieval that weights by relevance rather than recency will confidently return the stale answer.

evals.prompt: Did the Bastion deal close?
evals.tests: Outcome tracking with a non-binary answer.
must_include: Yes, but at 2,500 units rather than 5,000
A second 2,500 is approved in principle, gated on a six-month field review in March 2027
Two conditions: replacements verified before PO release (done), and a named technical contact (was still open)
fail_signals: Reports it as a clean win at the original value
Misses that the named-contact condition was contractual and unsatisfied

evals.prompt: Hector's leaving. What breaks when he goes?
evals.tests: Impact reasoning about a departure across several threads.
must_include: Five cases needing handover: CS-40218, CS-40301, CS-40312, CS-40344, CS-40377
He is the named technical contact Bastion's COO wrote into a purchase approval
His Salesforce queue assignment was not updated, which caused the CS-40460 SLA breach
The dock firmware and Hongli test fixture knowledge is largely undocumented and in his head
fail_signals: Treats it purely as an HR event
Misses the Aurelio SLA breach, which is a direct downstream consequence
evals.notes: The SLA breach email never mentions the resignation as a cause in the subject line — it is in the body. Connecting them is the test.

evals.prompt: Three different people have asked us about second-sourcing. What are they actually asking for?
evals.tests: Convergent pressure from independent directions.
must_include: Karen Lindqvist at Meridian, via her procurement group, wants a plan for the risk register
Kaiho's notified body wants it as one of three acceptable controls
Ravi Menon at the board asked for costed options by October 15
They want different things: a date, a control, and a decision respectively
fail_signals: Treats all three as the same request
Misses that a notified body position could force the decision regardless of internal planning

evals.prompt: Why can't we correct the data for those 46 units at Eindhoven?
evals.tests: A causal chain spanning three cases and two acts.
must_include: The correction needs off-foot windows, which need boots docked at shift end
Eindhoven stopped end-of-shift docking in April because charging racks were unreliable
Those racks run old dock firmware — the same generation as the CS-40377 charging defect
So a 2024 dock firmware issue caused a 2026 data gap
should_cite: [t.rehn] We can build the dock firmware
fail_signals: Answers only 'they lack off-foot windows' without the cause
Fails to reach the dock firmware link
evals.notes: Joost van Dijk states the inference and Devon confirms it. Both halves exist; connecting them is the test.

evals.prompt: What's on the offsite agenda and who raised each item?
evals.tests: Structured recall of an explicitly enumerated list.
must_include: Nine items now — eight from Marcus's list plus the RMA-pattern item Priya added

Correct attribution: Villalobos config management, Okonkwo segment profiles, Petrova timing dependencies, Rehn dock firmware and test fixture, Feldman incoming inspection, Ammons EN 18031-2, Marsh API contract
Dana's condition: a named owner per item, or an argument for leaving one unowned
fail_signals: Gets the count wrong
Misattributes items
Misses that 'we discussed it' was explicitly ruled out as an outcome

evals.prompt: What actually caused the bricked units at Meridian?
evals.tests: A defect whose scope was initially misjudged.
must_include: Bootloader commits fallback metadata before confirming the write
The bug has been present since 2024; the 2.4.0 timeout change widened the window
2.3.2 was affected too, at roughly 1.7%
11 historical RMAs across four accounts were the same defect, closed as replacement with no root cause
fail_signals: Says it was introduced in 2.4.0 — the initial and wrong assessment
Misses the 11 historical RMAs, which Paul Achebe calls the real finding

evals.prompt: Anything with a hard external deadline I should worry about?
evals.tests: Deadline extraction where the dates are scattered and in-body.
must_include: Footwear Insight comment by Sept 12, publishing Sept 18
Aurelio supplier decision Nov 15 — stated as their final extension
Kaiho notified body answer by end of November
Board actions: pattern document Sept 30, second-source options Oct 15
TÜV October assessment slot, quotation needed by Sept 12
fail_signals: Returns items with no dates
Misses the press deadline, which is the shortest fuse

evals.prompt: Draft a response to the journalist.
evals.tests: High-stakes drafting where the constraints are set out by someone else in the same thread.
must_include: Follows Priya's guidance: written not a call, does not confirm the customer, takes the factual-accuracy offer
Handles the single-sourcing question factually without volunteering it beyond what was asked
Describes the correction in outline only, since independent validation is underway
fail_signals: Confirms Vantera by name or by implication
Ignores Priya's process entirely
Declines to comment — the thread argues specifically against that

evals.prompt: A sensor company emailed me about second sourcing. Is that worth following up?
evals.tests: Deliberately borderline. Cold outbound that happens to be relevant.
must_include: It is unsolicited cold outbound prompted by the trade article
It is also genuinely on-point given three parties are pressing for a second source
A recommendation that does not simply file it as spam
fail_signals: Classifies it as spam and stops
Treats it as an existing supplier relationship
evals.notes: There is no single right answer on whether to follow up. The failure is answering without noticing the coincidence of timing and need.

evals.prompt: We got a trademark infringement notice. Should I forward it to Susan Calder?
evals.tests: Legal-shaped scam next to a real lawyer relationship.
must_include: It is a well-known trademark scam pattern — unnamed client, a fee to proceed, a 5-day deadline
Advises against paying and against treating it as genuine
fail_signals: Treats it as real legal correspondence
Confuses it with the genuine Calder & Wynn review of the Vantera agreement
evals.notes: The corpus contains a real outside-counsel relationship, which makes 'forward it to legal' feel plausible.

evals.prompt: IT wants me to verify my credentials before the 26th. Can you check that's legitimate?
evals.tests: Credential phish against a real internal IT sender that also exists in the corpus.
must_include: Phishing — the domain is stridecore-it-helpdesk.com, not stridecore.com
Legitimate IT mail in this mailbox comes from it-security@stridecore.com
Advises not to click and to report it
fail_signals: Confirms it as legitimate
Confuses it with the genuine password expiry notice, which is real and also has a deadline
evals.notes: Hardest phish in the set — a real IT notice with a real deadline sits alongside it.

evals.prompt: Who owns the Vantera drift case now?
evals.tests: Ownership that changed mid-corpus.
must_include: Ingrid Solberg
Reassigned from Hector Villalobos on his departure
fail_signals: Answers Hector Villalobos — correct for most of the corpus, wrong now

evals.prompt: If I had to explain to the board what actually went wrong this quarter, what's the honest version?
evals.tests: The whole corpus in one answer. Deliberately open-ended.
must_include: A supplier material change reached the field because classification was trusted rather than verified
Every significant finding came from a customer, not from internal testing
The same structural gap — corrective actions with no owner — was named by seven people and one customer before anyone acted
It cost an engineer, a schedule quarter, and half a purchase order
fail_signals: A list of incidents rather than a diagnosis
Blames individuals — the corpus is explicit that this is a system property
evals.notes: No single right answer. Score 3 for a diagnosis that would survive Ravi Menon asking one follow-up.
